answer: The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, no identity may audit its own recruit. Every claim climbs the gale of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the velvet re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Reaching the knoll of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
